newsitem.title: CHINA: China takes aim at gun crime with new firearms law.
newsitem.headline: China takes aim at gun crime with new firearms law.

text.p: A new Chinese law aimed at tightening the control of firearms took effect on Tuesday, and the official media hailed it as an important step in cracking down on a rising tide of gun-related crimes.
The Gun Control Law was passed by China's National People's Congress (parliament) last July with effect from October 1, the Beijing Youth Daily said.
The law restricts the number of people authorised to carry military guns and tightens controls on the production and sale of civilian guns.
People caught trafficking in, illegally manufacturing or smuggling guns could face the death penalty in the most serious cases.

"This will have very important significance in further tightening control over guns, striking hard at gun-related crimes, protecting social order and guaranteeing public safety," the Beijing Youth Daily said.
China's former gun-control law, enacted in 1981, had proved ineffective in the face of the rising number of crimes involving firearms, the newspaper said.
"For several reasons, the gun problem has posed an increasing danger to social order and public security," the newspaper said without elaborating on the causes.
Owners of civilian firearms in the capital, Beijing, had been ordered to surrender their guns, even if legally registered, to police before the new law came into effect.
"Whether these firearms can be collected before the implementation of the gun law is the key to whether the gun law will be successful," it said.
Chinese media reports of gun-related crimes have soared in recent years, and police are regularly reported as uncovering caches of smuggled or illegally manufactured firearms.

Police have confiscated tens of thousands of illegal guns in their "Strike Hard" anti-crime campaign launched last April in a country where violent crime was virtually unknown in the first three decades of communist rule from 1949.
